The term Remnant is the app's own key term and is defined at the step that carries it.

7 words, one sentence. "Earliest covering requires death of an animal" states one claim with a subject and a verb; "covering" is the everyday word for what Gen 3:21 describes. No decode word and no separator.

3 words, one sentence. "Abel's firstlings accepted" is a nominal title for Gen 4:4; "firstlings" is the verse's own word ("of the firstlings of his flock"), so modernising it would break I1, and the step's connection immediately glosses what it means (the firstborn animal given by blood).

6 words, one sentence. "God will provide Himself the lamb" is Gen 22:8 verbatim ("My son, God will provide himself a lamb for a burnt offering"); the served KJV confirms it, so it is Scripture carried with no quotation marks, and every word of it is untouchable under I1.

6 words, one sentence. "blood on doorposts averts death" names the sign, the place and the outcome in one idea. "averts" is the only word above everyday register, and both the step title and the Exodus setting make it concrete; the parallel connection at step 0 now uses the plainer "turned death away".
2 words, one sentence. "Passover lamb" is the plainest possible label for Exod 12:3-13 and is the term the reader will meet everywhere else; expanding a 2-word title would pad it.

5 words, one sentence. "Behold the Lamb of God" is John 1:29's own words ("Behold the Lamb of God, which taketh away the sin of the world"); it is Scripture carried unquoted, so "Behold" must not be modernised to "Look" under I1.

7 words, one sentence. "He did not spare His own Son" is the app's own unquoted rendering of Rom 8:32 (served KJV: "He that spared not his own son"). CP-02 §6 records this exact example as a loose rendering that writers flag but never silently correct, so it is carried byte-identical.

4 words, one sentence. "Lamb without blemish, foreknown" is a two-part nominal title for 1 Pet 1:19-20; "without blemish" is the verse's wording and "foreknown" is the one decode word, which the connection beneath it now states plainly as "chose this unblemished sacrifice before the world began".

Chain display label, 4 words. "Provided Lamb / Substitution" uses the chain's own two key terms and the slash is the app's own device; the second term is the technical one, but the chain's first step explains it (an animal died in place of the son) and the label is the navigation handle readers search by.

6 words, one sentence. "First rain and latter rain promised" is the app's own label for Deut 11:14, which names both rains in one line. The served KJV confirms the pair ("the first rain and the latter rain"), so the terms are the verse's and there is no decode word or citation to move.

9 words, one sentence. "He shall come as the rain to the earth" is Hos 6:3's own clause ("he shall come unto us as the rain"); the served KJV confirms it, so it is unquoted Scripture carried byte-identical under I1, pronoun capitalisation included.

9 words, one sentence. "Former rain and latter rain in the first month" is Joel 2:23's own wording ("the former rain, and the latter rain in the first month"); the served KJV confirms it, and "the first month" is Scripture's time marker, not a numeral this sweep may touch.

7 words, one sentence. "Pour out My Spirit on all flesh" is Joel 2:28 verbatim; the served KJV confirms it, the capital "My" is inside the verse's own clause, and it is the same Scripture clause the day-of-the-lord chain opens with, so its wording must not diverge between the two chains.

9 words, one sentence. "Ask rain in the time of the latter rain" is Zech 10:1's own wording (served KJV: "Ask ye of the LORD rain in the time of the latter rain"); it is unquoted Scripture carried byte-identical, so the imperative "Ask" stays and no citation or numeral is involved.

7 words plus the leading label "Pentecost:". Both halves are already plain and the label is the app's own marker; "The Early Rain of the Spirit" is the chain's own coined title for Pentecost, so capitalisation is deliberate and changing it would be a naming change, not a clarity fix.

8 words, one sentence. "Be patient until the early and latter rain" is James 5:7's own wording (served KJV: "until he receive the early and latter rain"); the served text confirms both terms, so it is unquoted Scripture carried and the imperative "Be patient" must not be modernised.

7 words plus a parenthetical label. "Earth lightened with His glory" is Rev 18:1's own wording (served KJV: "the earth was lightened with his glory"); "Loud Cry" is the app's own named label for the final outpouring and the parenthesis is the app's device, so both are carried and nothing needs decoding.

Chain display label, 8 words. "The Early and Latter Rain of the Spirit" names both rains and the Spirit in the plainest form the chain's key terms allow; it matches the chain id and the step titles beneath it, so no change is warranted.

12 words, one sentence, one idea. "modeled after" is a plain verb and the sentence names both the earthly building and the heavenly reality it copies, which is what Exod 25:40 states. The one word above everyday register, "blueprint", is glossed by the phrase right after it ("earthly tabernacle").

9 words plus a colon. "Pattern of the Sanctuary: God dwells with His people" is clear in both halves, and in this chain the colon is a structural leading marker rather than a mid-sentence dip, so it is kept. The key term "Sanctuary" is named and at once explained as where God dwells.

6 words, one sentence. "Heavenly court seated and books opened" is a compressed image but each word is everyday and it matches Dan 7:10 exactly ("the judgment was set, and the books were opened"); at 6 words there is no long clause for a rewrite to relieve.

13 words, one sentence. Names Christ as the minister, the place (heaven itself) and quotes the distinction that matters ("which the Lord pitched and not man", Heb 8:2, carried byte-identical). One idea, active verb, no decode word beyond "pitched", which the verse itself uses.

7 words, one sentence. "Christ High Priest of the true tabernacle" is Heb 8:1-2's own terms; the missing article is a title convention used throughout this chain ("Christ minister of the true tabernacle" at the sister chain) and inserting one would change the app's title style rather than its clarity.

12 words, one sentence, one idea. Names the place (the Most Holy Place), the cause (the seventh trumpet) and the event (it is opened). Left byte-identical deliberately: this string is shared byte-for-byte with chain:sanctuary-judgment|steps[6].connection, and the one-writer rule (§1.12) means both occurrences must move together or not at all. It stays because this chain is the number-dense one and "seventh" must not be disturbed; the identical string appears in the sanctuary-judgment chain's worklist, where the same owner can revisit both at once.

Chain display label, 8 words plus a leading "1.". The leading numeral is part of the label and must not be dropped or renumbered; "The 2,300 Days & Cleansing of the Sanctuary" carries the chain's numeral byte-identical and names the event. This is the one chain name I considered changing, and I am leaving it because the numeral and the ampersand are the app's navigation identity for this pillar.

6 words, one sentence. "Bronze serpent set upon a pole" is a passive nominal title but every word is everyday and it matches Num 21:8-9's own picture ("set it upon a pole"); no decode word and no separator.

4 words, one sentence. "Nehushtan broken in pieces" carries the Hebrew name Nehushtan and the phrase "brake in pieces" from 2 Kgs 18:4; Hebrew names and transliterations are untouchable under I1 and the step's connection explains the event, so the title is left as-is.

10 words, one sentence. "Even so must the Son of Man be lifted up" is John 3:14 verbatim ("even so must the Son of man be lifted up"); it is Scripture carried unquoted, so the archaic verb order must not be modernised.

8 words, one sentence. "When you lift up the Son of Man" is John 8:28's own clause ("When ye have lifted up the Son of man"); the served KJV confirms it and "the Son of Man" is a title that must stay byte-identical, so the only variance is the pronoun, which I1 tells me to carry.

8 words, one sentence. "Lifted up from the earth to draw all" is John 12:32's own words ("if I be lifted up from the earth, will draw all men unto me") compressed to a title; no decode word, no citation, and the compression is the verse's own phrasing rather than an abstraction.

4 words, one sentence. "Made sin for us" is 2 Cor 5:21's own words ("he hath made him to be sin for us"); the served KJV confirms it, so it is unquoted Scripture carried and the missing subject is supplied by the connection beneath it.
Chain display label, 6 words. "The Bronze Serpent and the Cross" names both ends of the chain in everyday words and matches the chain id; nothing in it needs decoding and it is not unclear.
